summary: The Sylvester-Hadamard family A_k=H^(tensor k) has all eigenvalues of modulus one and contains an explicit three-large-eigenvector frame whose maximum coordinate leverage tends to zero, but every fixed r x r physical principal block has operator norm at most r/sqrt(n), tending to zero. Thus delocalization of three large eigenvectors does not force a uniformly nondegenerate bounded-size principal block. This does not refute QFORM: the same family has a global original-coordinate cross block BB^T=(1/2)I and is uniformly controlled by the completed ridge theorem with density at most e for n>=16.
